One step's rainfall field on a grid

Source: R/rainfall_merge.R
rainfall_field.Rd

The field merge_rainfall() averages over the catchment, for one time step and every cell of the grid: for mapping a storm, or for seeing what each method does to it.

Usage

rainfall_field(
  gauges,
  values,
  grid,
  method = c("multiquadric", "conditional", "thiessen"),
  c = NULL,
  smooth = 0,
  radar = NULL
)

Arguments

gauges

Data frame of gauges with columns id, x and y (projected coordinates, such as British National Grid metres).

values

One step's gauge depths, mm, in the order of gauges; NA leaves a gauge out.

grid

List with x and y, the cell-centre coordinates of the grid's columns and rows.

method

thiessen, multiquadric or conditional.

c

Multiquadric shape parameter; by default the median distance between neighbouring gauges.

smooth

Nonnegative smoothing added to the diagonal of the multiquadric system, in the units of the basis (coordinate units); 0 passes exactly through the gauges.

radar

With method = "conditional", that step's radar grid, mm: a matrix of length(grid$x) rows by length(grid$y) columns.

Value

A matrix of rain, mm, with length(grid$x) rows and length(grid$y) columns.

See also

merge_rainfall()

Examples

grid <- list(x = seq(500, 9500, by = 1000), y = seq(500, 9500, by = 1000))
gauges <- data.frame(id = 1:4, x = c(2000, 8000, 2000, 8000), y = c(2000, 2000, 8000, 8000))
field <- rainfall_field(gauges, c(1, 4, 2, 0), grid, method = "multiquadric")
image(grid$x, grid$y, field)
